subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is a dwarf brawler who accepts ranged roles out of necessity, wields a crossbow reluctantly, and holds Dawnbringer as his true weapon; he respects tactical leverage and operates through terrain and position.
source_quote: I'm standing on a bridge over a pit that smells like the inside of a dying thing... I take it, because I'd rather be in the fight badly than out of it entirely.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir executes the pivotal teleport-and-grapple maneuver to drop Ilvara into the Heart Fungus's damage zone, demonstrating precision and control over battlefield geometry.
source_quote: I can try to grab Ilvara and drop her into that, such that you're hurting both of them, and then the rest of you can fireball or whatever from there.

subject: Jorlan
fact: Jorlan is a humiliated former follower of Ilvara, consumed by rage, standing directly on the Glyph of Warding unaware — his predictable emotional vector is exploited by Thorin to trigger a decisive area denial effect.
source_quote: He's across the cavern, bitter-eyed, nursing whatever wound his pride has taken since Ilvara discarded him.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum placed the Glyph of Warding on the bridge with deliberate patience, creating a hidden tactical trap that becomes instrumental in disrupting Ilvara’s reinforcements.
source_quote: Jorlan is standing exactly twenty feet from the Glyph of Warding that Grygum spent real patience setting into the stone of the bridge.

subject: Velkynvelve
fact: Velkynvelve was once a guard force now corrupted into spore servants, reanimated by Ilvara’s fungal influence to serve as frontline shock troops in the battle.
source_quote: Four of them, former Velkynvelve guards, shambling and wrong.

subject: Heart Fungus
fact: The Heart Fungus is a sentient, pulsing fungal entity that controls Ilvara, emits lethal spore clouds, and reforms her after damage — it acts as both a living mechanism and a hostile environmental hazard.
source_quote: The Heart Fungus pulsed between us and her, enormous and obscene, the mechanism of her control... It unleashes a cloud of spores that hits Zalthir so hard he has to climb ten feet straight up just to breathe.

subject: Spore Servants
fact: Spore Servants are reanimated former Velkynvelve guards, shambling and corrupted by fungal growth, emerging from the ground to reinforce Ilvara’s defenses during combat.
source_quote: Four of them, former Velkynvelve guards, shambling and wrong.

subject: Dawnbringer
fact: Dawnbringer is Thorin’s enchanted sword, a weapon of radiant light that defies the darkness of the cavern, wielded only when Thorin closes to melee — it symbolizes his true role as a frontline warrior.
source_quote: I have Dawnbringer in hand — the real hand, the right hand, the one that knows what it's doing... The blade catches some ambient light... and turns it into something brighter, something that has no business existing this deep underground.

subject: Light Crossbow
fact: The light crossbow is lent to Thorin as a temporary ranged tool, used only because he lacks better options — it represents his compromise between identity and necessity.
source_quote: Someone lends me a crossbow, and I take it, because I'd rather be in the fight badly than out of it entirely.

subject: Glyph of Warding
fact: The Glyph of Warding is a hidden magical trap placed by Grygum on the bridge, designed to detonate when triggered — it is the key tactical element that disrupts Ilvara’s reinforcement strategy.
source_quote: Jorlan is standing exactly twenty feet from the Glyph of Warding that Grygum spent real patience setting into the stone of the bridge.

subject: Dust of Suleiman
fact: The Dust of Suleiman is a magical substance used to burn the Heart Fungus, targeting its control infrastructure rather than Ilvara’s illusions — chosen for strategic efficacy over emotional satisfaction.
source_quote: The Dust of Suleiman burns the Heart Fungus... because Asha was right and the infrastructure was more important than the satisfying image of Ilvara's nightmares eating her alive.

subject: teleport-grapple-drop
fact: Zalthir teleports into position, grapples Ilvara, and drops her into the Heart Fungus’s damage zone, initiating the core tactical sequence of the battle.
source_quote: Zalthir vanishes — just gone, teleported straight to her — and then there's the crack of his fists finding purchase, once, twice, thirty-one damage in the space of a breath.

subject: glyph detonation
fact: Jorlan charges onto the Glyph of Warding, triggering a 21-damage explosion that destroys one spore servant, cripples another, and destabilizes the Heart Fungus — a decisive shift in battlefield dynamics.
source_quote: He comes straight onto the bridge, straight onto the glyph, and the detonation is immediate and total — 21 damage, one spore servant gone to nothing, another barely holding itself together, and the Heart Fungus itself shuddering from the force of it.

subject: Ilvara's true form
fact: Ilvara’s transformation into a fungal entity raises unresolved questions about her original identity, the nature of her corruption, and whether she retains any vestige of self beneath the Heart Fungus’s control.
source_quote: She was on an elevated platform. Corrupted. The fungal growth had changed her in ways that were specific and terrible — the scourge still in her hand, but everything else altered.

subject: Jorlan's redemption
fact: Jorlan’s rage-driven charge may have been exploited, but his emotional state and survival leave open the question of whether he can be saved — or if he will become another casualty of Ilvara’s corruption.
source_quote: He's armed. He's furious. He's also standing exactly twenty feet from the Glyph of Warding... He's been stewing in it so long the rot has gone all the way through.

subject: Cavern of the Heart Fungus
fact: The cavern is a corrupted subterranean space dominated by the pulsing Heart Fungus, with elevated platforms, fungal growths, and hidden glyphs — terrain that is actively hostile and dynamically reshaped by Ilvara’s will.
source_quote: We watched Ilvara from the corridor near the pools... The cavern is full in a way that starts to feel personal.

subject: Bridge of Warding
fact: The bridge spans a pit over the cavern, bearing the Glyph of Warding placed by Grygum — it is the focal point of the ambush, where Jorlan’s charge triggers the decisive tactical moment.
source_quote: Jorlan is standing exactly twenty feet from the Glyph of Warding that Grygum spent real patience setting into the stone of the bridge.

subject: session date
fact: The events occur during the current session, immediately following the planning phase and leading directly into the execution of the assassination plan.
source_quote: Now we just had to survive the execution.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz coordinates the tactical phases of the battle — opening volley, spell depletion, brawler entry — and later executes a fireball to strike the overlap zone, demonstrating battlefield awareness and timing.
source_quote: Daz talked through the phases — the opening volley, the depletion of spell slots, the point at which the brawlers would need to go in... Daz fireballs the overlap.

subject: Asha
fact: Asha advocated for targeting the Heart Fungus’s infrastructure over emotional or symbolic destruction — her strategic insight directly influenced the choice to use the Dust of Suleiman.
source_quote: because Asha was right and the infrastructure was more important than the satisfying image of Ilvara's nightmares eating her alive.

subject: Thorin's identity conflict
fact: Thorin struggles between his identity as a brawler and the tactical necessity of ranged combat — his internal conflict is resolved not by changing his nature, but by accepting his role as leverage in a larger machine.
source_quote: I made peace with it before the fight started. Mostly.

subject: the fungal takeover
fact: The transformation of Ilvara and the environment into fungal constructs suggests a deeper, possibly sentient corruption — raising questions about whether the Heart Fungus is a tool, a parasite, or a new form of life.
source_quote: The fungal growth had changed her in ways that were specific and terrible — the scourge still in her hand, but everything else altered.
